attacks.claim: The 5-minute freshness check depends on the host clock. On self-hosted hardware without NTP or an RTC, drift beyond 5 minutes makes every delivery fail with a silent 401. The only signal is a warning log, and no metric or alert is added.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no metric, alert, or documented NTP/clock requirement. Artifact says: "rejects deliveries more than 5 minutes old or in the future, and returns a bare 401"

attacks.claim: Upgrading requires the operator to provision the vendor secret before the new version can ingest anything. The PR does not say whether the vendor retries 401s, so readings sent during a misconfigured window may be lost.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: documented vendor retry policy for rejected deliveries. Artifact says: "New required env vars are announced in release notes"

attacks.claim: A captured valid delivery can be replayed anywhere in the 5-minute window. There is no nonce or delivery-ID dedupe. The idempotent upsert limits the damage, but a replayed older batch could overwrite a newer corrected value if the upsert is last-write-wins.
attacks.evidence: "rejects deliveries more than 5 minutes old or in the future"; no nonce or delivery-ID check appears in signing.py

attacks.claim: The full body is read into memory before authentication, and the app enforces no size limit. Safety depends entirely on the proxy cap, which self-hosted deployments may not have.
attacks.evidence: "body = await request.body()" with "the reverse proxy caps request bodies at 1 MB"

attacks.claim: The get_db dependency resolves before the signature check, so unauthenticated requests still acquire a database handle. This amplifies the cost of unauthenticated floods.
attacks.evidence: "async def plugcloud_webhook(request: Request, db: Database = Depends(get_db), ...)"

attacks.claim: The secret check is length-only. A low-entropy value such as "a"*32 passes the validator and would make HMAC forgery feasible.
The claim that startup fails when the secret is missing depends on where Settings is instantiated. The diff does not show get_settings or any eager construction, so the claim is unverified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: definition of get_settings and any startup-time Settings() call. Artifact says: "startup fails if it is missing or short"

attacks.claim: Header parsing is lenient. removeprefix accepts a bare hex value with no v1= prefix, and multi-signature headers (needed during secret rotation) are not handled.
